answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when its behavior is proven to violate a fraud rule, with evidence and appeals handled by a bonded validator quorum. A single attacker can still mint many keys, but must lock real capital for each one and risks losing it; spreading identities does not dilute that cost. For example, an opal-market agent might flag a falcon account’s coordinated plume of sham bids, prompting review rather than automatic punishment.
